llm.summary: The skill mostly fits its stated purpose (deploy a Portal + local Bridge) but the package contains hard-coded secrets, example credentials, and unrelated API keys/notes, and its runtime instructions ask the agent to read/write local sensitive config and to SSH+deploy—these inconsistencies warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Agent P2P Portal + send.py) align with the files and instructions: scripts for deploying a Portal on a VPS, a local Bridge, send.py/send_file.py, and docs about API keys and shared keys. Requiring an SSH key, Portal URL and OpenClaw hooks token is coherent for automated VPS deployment and bridge setup. However, the repository also contains unrelated or sensitive items (hard-coded tokens and personal memory files) that do not belong to a clean, shareable skill release.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and auto_install.py instruct the agent to read local OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, gateway.env), write ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, SSH into a VPS, clone/run code on remote, and manage systemd/nginx—these are powerful, legitimate for deployment but inherently sensitive. The instructions require reading/writing local files containing secrets (hooks token, admin creds), and include commands that will place admin credentials on the local machine. The SKILL.md also enforces using send.py for messaging and describes file uploads that allow direct upload to remote portals without confirmation—this is a design choice but raises privacy concerns.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec in registry metadata (instruction-only), but many code files are included. auto_install.py executes remote shell scripts via SSH and clones a GitHub repo; deploy scripts create systemd services and call certbot. These are typical for a self-hosted app but have high impact (remote execution via SSH, system service changes). The code pulls from a GitHub repo (traceable), not from shorteners or unknown binary hosts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared required env vars (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) match the skill's functionality. Concern: OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and SSH private key grant broad ability to wake and control the local agent and remote VPS respectively—they are high-value secrets and should be scoped carefully. Additionally, the repository contains unrelated secret-like items (e.g., TOOLS.md includes an external Bearer token; MEMORY.md contains VPS IP, SSH key path, admin password and example API keys). Those hard-coded secrets are not proportional and indicate either accidental leakage or sloppy publishing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and allows normal autonomous invocation. It does instruct creating persistent files under ~/.openclaw (gateway.env, agent-p2p-admin.txt) and creating systemd services on the remote VPS, which is expected for a deployer skill. This persistence is powerful but coherent with the stated purpose.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements a self-hosted Portal + local Bridge and thus legitimately needs SSH access, a Portal API key and the OpenClaw hooks token. However: 1) The package contains hard-coded/example secrets (API tokens, admin password, VPS IP/SSH key paths) — that suggests the author accidentally published private data; DO NOT trust those values. 2) Before installing, review the repo (especially MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, AGENTS.md and any .env/.json files) and remove any hard-coded tokens or secrets. 3) Never provide your primary SSH private key or global hooks token — create a dedicated low-permission SSH key and a limited hooks token. 4) Do not run auto_install.py or deploy scripts unattended; run them step-by-step in a controlled environment (or on an isolated VM) so you can inspect each SSH command that will run on your VPS. 5) Verify the upstream GitHub repo and contact the maintainer; if the package includes other services or third-party API keys (like the bearer token in TOOLS.md), ask why they are included and rotate any tokens you exposed. 6) If you proceed, rotate credentials (owner/shared keys, hooks tokens) after installation and monitor the VPS for unexpected outgoing connections or changes.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A base64-block pattern was detected in SKILL.md pre-scan. auto_install.py uses `openssl rand -base64` to generate admin passwords which could trigger the pattern detector; however presence of base64-encoded blobs in repo or docs is unexpected and should be inspected to ensure they are not hidden payloads or embedded secrets.
